heroHeadline: Warsh Sworn In at White House (First Since Greenspan 1987); Flash PMI: Mfg 55.3 (4-Year High) vs Services 50.9 — Stagflation Split; S&P +0.55%, 30Y Eases to ~5.09%; Q2 GDP Trajectory ~1%
heroSubtitle: On Friday May 22, 2026 — Kevin Warsh's first day as the formally sworn-in 17th Federal Reserve Chair — the US economy sent deeply conflicting signals that encapsulate the stagflation trap Warsh now must navigate. At 11 a.m. EDT, Warsh was sworn in at the White House in the first Fed Chair ceremony held there since Alan Greenspan's swearing-in in 1987 — a symbolically charged venue that market watchers noted signals the administration's close alignment with its chosen Chair. The macroeconomic inheritance on Day 8 (operational) / Day 1 (official): CPI 3.8% YoY (April), PPI +6.0% YoY (April — hottest since December 2022), Core PCE 3.2% (March), and FOMC April minutes explicitly showing officials discussed raising interest rates. S&P Global's Flash PMI May 2026 report (released May 22) confirmed the bifurcated economy Warsh inherits: Manufacturing PMI surged to 55.3 — the highest since May 2022 (a 48-month high) — driven by front-loaded inventory rebuilding and AI capex, while Services PMI slipped to 50.9 (a 2-month low), with S&P Global warning the Composite PMI of 51.7 implies Q2 GDP growth of only approximately 1% annualized — a dramatic deceleration from Q1 2026's +2.0% advance estimate. Critically, input cost pressures accelerated in both sectors simultaneously: manufacturing input prices rose at the fastest pace since June 2022, and services price increases were the fastest in a year — meaning the inflation pipeline is strengthening, not easing, precisely as the economy approaches near-stall speed. Weekly initial jobless claims (209,000, fell 3,000 from prior week) held at historically resilient levels, providing the only clean positive data point of the session. Financial markets responded favorably to one tactical development: Iran peace talks facilitated by the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar generated sufficient optimism to ease the 30-year Treasury yield to approximately 5.086% from Monday's 18-year high of 5.189%, pushing the S&P 500 +0.55%, the Dow Jones +0.74% toward a fresh record, and the Russell 2000 +0.93%. Brent crude settled at approximately $104.52–$105/barrel (+1.9%), still elevated near $105 — the Iran conflict's supply disruption persists, with the IEA having warned the global oil market will remain severely undersupplied until at least October 2026 even if fighting ends immediately. The structural recession risk factors remain fully intact: Moody's Aa1 sovereign downgrade (May 16, completing the clean sweep of all three agencies), the Federal Circuit stay on the Section 122 tariff legal challenge keeping tariffs active but legally precarious toward the July 23 cliff (62 days), Goldman at 30%, JPMorgan at 35%, and Moody's Analytics at 49% recession probabilities — all compiled before the FOMC minutes rate hike signal and before the Flash PMI confirmed Q2 near-stall speed.
footerNote: Data sourced from S&P Global Flash US PMI (Manufacturing 55.3, Services 50.9, Composite 51.7, released May 22, 2026), Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance (Warsh sworn in at White House May 22 at 11 a.m. EDT), CNBC (Treasury yields: 30Y ~5.086%, 10Y ~4.564%, May 22), TheStreet (S&P +0.55%, Dow +0.74%, Nasdaq +0.53%, Russell +0.93%, May 22), Fortune (Brent crude ~$104.52, May 22), GV Wire / WTVB (weekly jobless claims 209K, May 22), Goldman Sachs / JPMorgan / Moody's Analytics (recession probabilities 30%, 35%, 49%).
